verdict.rationale: The SFU API controls which endpoints receive audio, video and data. Any WebSocket server, such as an agent in a Durable Object, can receive live call audio as PCM and video as JPEG without a WebRTC client, and publications exist independently of subscribers. The evidence never explicitly describes picking one specific track from a broadcast, or states that the publisher's setup stays untouched; video egress is also limited to JPEG at about 1 FPS. Missing for 10: explicit per-track subscription documentation, an explicit guarantee that the publisher needs no changes, full-rate video for agents, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent subscribes to a single track of a live broadcast without the publisher changing anything about how it publishes

citations.quote: Use the Realtime SFU API to control which endpoints publish or receive audio, video, and data.
Any server that accepts WebSockets, such as a Durable Object, can receive live call audio as PCM samples and video as JPEG frames without implementing a WebRTC client.
Traffic published into Cloudflare is free, including when no client subscribes to that publication.
